record: CLOSED: the Thor DiT anomaly is a roofline effect -- predicted to 1.1% from independently measured hardware roofs -- plus one mis-selected kernel worth 14%
closes: the then-undiagnosed Thor DiT anomaly carried in groot_compiled_fleet_2026-08-27.json

measured_hardware_roofs.roof_validation: Orin's LLM GEMMs hit 30.56 TFLOP/s against the 30.32 measured roof — 100.8%

arithmetic_intensity.dit_detail: 1097 MB of weights for only 70.7 GFLOP of work. It sits 4.9x BELOW Thor's ridge point of 316.

mechanism_1_dominant_dit_is_dram_weight_.key_measurement: Thor's DiT GEMMs run at 261.5 GB/s = 99.3% OF THOR'S MEASURED DRAM ROOF, and 12.9% of its compute roof. It is pinned to memory.
mechanism_1_dominant_dit_is_dram_weight_.why_thor_specifically: Thor has 2.75x Orin's COMPUTE but only 1.52x its BANDWIDTH. So a compute-bound stage tracks 2.75 and a memory-bound stage tracks 1.52. Measured Thor/Orin: ViT 2.57x (compute), LLM 2.15x (AI 296 ~ Thor's ridge 316, in between), DiT 1.41x (bandwidth). THAT SPLIT IS THE ANOMALY.

prediction.from: independently measured roofs only, no fitting
prediction.calc: Orin's DiT/ViT 0.654 x (compute ratio 2.749 / bandwidth ratio 1.523)
prediction.significance: this PREDICTS the anomaly rather than fitting it. The mechanism is closed.

mechanism_1_dominant_dit_is_dram_weight_.confirmed_by_controlled_probe: the DiT's own GEMM shape (302 MB weights) with only M varying, M=1 -> 49 — i.e. 49x the arithmetic for the SAME bytes — costs Thor only +8.1%, the 5090 +12.3%, Orin +1.1%. The math is nearly free; the bytes are everything. This also rules occupancy out BY EXPERIMENT rather than by inference.

mechanism_2_secondary_14pct_one_mis_sele.layer: the vl_embs batched K/V projection [1,296,2048] x [16,2048,1536] -> [16,296,1536]
mechanism_2_secondary_14pct_one_mis_sele.isolated_repro: standalone engine 1.150 ms against a 0.382 ms roofline ceiling; excess 0.794 ms = 13.9% of Thor's DiT
mechanism_2_secondary_14pct_one_mis_sele.verdict: a genuine kernel-SELECTION defect, not a hardware limit — Thor picks a Blackwell-datacenter CUTLASS stream-K kernel where the two fast boards pick sm80 xmma. Fixing it would give Thor DiT/ViT 1.027, still 1.57x Orin's 0.654. Real but secondary; the roofline dominates.

ruled_out.launch_small_kernel: NO. GR00T on Thor: DiT 129 launches @ 47.0 us, ViT 192 @ 25.0 us — the DiT launches FEWER, LONGER kernels. Enqueue 0.354 ms (6.2% of compute) vs the ViT's 0.607 ms (12.7%).
ruled_out.sm80_fallback: NO. The 5090 and Orin use sm80_xmma kernels too, and those are the FAST ones.
ruled_out.fp32_accumulate: REAL BUT NOT BINDING. Thor's DiT spends 59.2% of its time in fp32-accum GEMMs vs 0% for its ViT — a true Thor+DiT-only asymmetry — but at 99.3% of the bandwidth roof and 12.9% of compute, accumulate rate cannot be the constraint.
ruled_out.memory_clock_throttling: NO. EMC pinned at 4266 MHz throughout both DiT and ViT runs, 44 C, pmode 0000.

correction_history.superseded_hypothesis: 'the DiT launches 3.2x MORE kernels than the ViT, each 3.1x shorter -- a launch-overhead signature', from ncu CSVs on Thor.
correction_history.why_it_was_wrong: those CSVs profiled another model's engines (202 MB DiT), not GR00T's (1102 MB DiT). Its kernel counts had been joined to GR00T's milliseconds, so the '11.4 us/kernel' figure was not a real quantity. Checking the profiled file paths exposed the mismatch.
correction_history.corrected_finding: for GR00T the DiT launches FEWER and LONGER kernels than the ViT (129 @ 47 us vs 192 @ 25 us).

published_thor_dit_figure_is_at_the_favo.what: today's re-measure put Thor's DiT at 5.39-5.84 ms across FIVE engine variants, against the 4.944 ms we published. ViT 4.79-4.90 vs 4.816; Orin (8.048/12.300) and the 5090 (1.314/1.820) reproduce our published figures exactly.
published_thor_dit_figure_is_at_the_favo.interpretation: within the known ~8-10% TensorRT build-to-build variance -- but 4.944 is almost exactly the 4.915 ms the DiT would take with the mis-selected kernel (mechanism 2) fixed, so that build plausibly drew a better tactic for the mis-selected layer.
published_thor_dit_figure_is_at_the_favo.consequence: our published Thor DiT is at the FAVOURABLE end of its build distribution. The anomaly is unaffected either way (DiT/ViT 1.03-1.19 on Thor versus 0.65-0.72 elsewhere), but the single figure should carry a range.
published_thor_dit_figure_is_at_the_favo.action: quote Thor's DiT as a range or as a median of builds, not as 4.944 alone.

still_open: why the cutlass3x_sm100 stream-K kernel stalls at 24% of roof is not explained at the microarchitectural level. ncu hardware counters need root on both Thor and the 5090 (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM), so there are no direct occupancy or tensor-op-utilisation numbers. Occupancy was ruled out by controlled experiment instead, which is sound but indirect; one ncu run as root on Thor would close it.
input_provenance: synthetic by construction for the roofline probes and the GEMM-shape sweep, where the shapes and byte counts ARE the independent variable and input content is irrelevant. The GR00T stage timings being explained use a recorded (simulated) GR1 observation from NVIDIA's demo_data/robot_sim.PickNPlace, not synthetic data.
